\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قضية} (qaḍiyya)}{قضية (qaḍiyya)}]{\ar{قضية} (qaḍiyya) — a public issue; a cause; a court case}

\label{lesson:AR-C361-qadiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to argue, then the Arabic for a controversy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قضية}}
\textbf{\ar{قضية}} — \emph{qaḍiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a public issue; a cause; a court case\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكلمنا} \ar{عن} \ar{قضية} \ar{الماء} \ar{في} \ar{القرية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takallamnā ʿan qaḍiyyat al-māʾ fī al-qarya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We talked about the issue of water in the village.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{قضايا}, \emph{qaḍāyā}. In a court it is a case.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قضية}} (\emph{qaḍiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-ḍ-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to decide, to settle\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{qaḍiyya} is a matter to be decided: a case, a cause, an issue.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaḍiyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaḍiyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takallamnā ʿan qaḍiyyat al-māʾ fī al-qarya.} — We talked about the issue of water in the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to argue, then the Arabic for a controversy, then say \emph{qaḍiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{قضية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A public issue; a cause; a court case\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مسألة} (masʾala)}{مسألة (masʾala)}]{\ar{مسألة} (masʾala) — a matter}

\label{lesson:AR-C361-masala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a controversy, then the Arabic for a public issue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مسألة}}
\textbf{\ar{مسألة}} — \emph{masʾala} — \textquotedblleft{}a matter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هذه} \ar{مسألة} \ar{صعبة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hādhihi masʾala ṣaʿba.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is a difficult matter.
\end{quote}

Also a problem in arithmetic: \ar{مسألة} \ar{حساب}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مسألة}} (\emph{masʾala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-ʾ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{masʾala} is a thing asked about: a question to settle, a matter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masʾala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masʾala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādhihi masʾala ṣaʿba.} — This is a difficult matter.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a controversy, then the Arabic for a public issue, then say \emph{masʾala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مسألة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A matter\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سياق} (siyāq)}{سياق (siyāq)}]{\ar{سياق} (siyāq) — a context}

\label{lesson:AR-C361-siyaq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a public issue, then the Arabic for a matter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سياق}}
\textbf{\ar{سياق}} — \emph{siyāq} — \textquotedblleft{}a context\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فهمت} \ar{معنى} \ar{الكلمة} \ar{من} \ar{السياق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fahimtu maʿnā al-kalima min as-siyāq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I understood the meaning of the word from the context.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سياق}} (\emph{siyāq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-w-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to drive along\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{siyāq} is a driving along in order; in modern use, the run of words around a word: its context.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a public issue, then the Arabic for a matter, then say \emph{siyāq} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أثار} (athāra)}{أثار (athāra)}]{\ar{أثار} (athāra) — to stir up; to raise}

\label{lesson:AR-C361-athara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a matter, then the Arabic for a context.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أثار}}
\textbf{\ar{أثار}} — \emph{athāra} — \textquotedblleft{}to stir up; to raise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أثار} \ar{الخبر} \ar{اهتمام} \ar{الناس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{athāra al-khabar ihtimām an-nās.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The news stirred up people's interest.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يثير}, \emph{yuthīr}.

\ar{أثار} \ar{مشكلة}, raised a problem.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أثار}} (\emph{athāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to rise up, to be stirred\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, to stir up: to raise dust, and so to raise feelings or a question.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a matter, then the Arabic for a context, then say \emph{athāra} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تساءل} (tasāʾala)}{تساءل (tasāʾala)}]{\ar{تساءل} (tasāʾala) — to wonder}

\label{lesson:AR-C361-tasaala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a context, then the Arabic for to stir up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تساءل}}
\textbf{\ar{تساءل}} — \emph{tasāʾala} — \textquotedblleft{}to wonder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تساءلت} \ar{أمي} \ar{عن} \ar{سبب} \ar{التأخير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tasāʾalat ummī ʿan sabab at-taʾkhīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother wondered about the reason for the delay.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتساءل}, \emph{yatasāʾal}.

Form VI of the root of \ar{سأل}, to ask: to ask oneself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تساءل}} (\emph{tasāʾala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-ʾ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI of \emph{saʾala}, \textquotedblleft{}to ask\textquotedblright{}: to ask oneself, to wonder.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasāʾala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasāʾalat ummī ʿan sabab at-taʾkhīr.} — My mother wondered about the reason for the delay.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a context, then the Arabic for to stir up, then say \emph{tasāʾala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
